source_text: Καὶ μὴ θαύμαζε, εἰ μὴ πάντες βλέπουσιν οἱ πεπιστευκότες ὄχλοι τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτοῦ· ὅτε ὡς μὴ χωροῦσι πλείονα Κορινθίοις ὁ Παῦλος γράφων φησίν· „ἐγὼ δὲ ἔκρινα μηδὲν εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον.“ τοιοῦτον δέ ἐστι καὶ τό· „οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε· ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε, ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε.“ οὕτω τοίνυν πάντα κρίσει θείᾳ ποιῶν ὁ λόγος ἀνέγραψε περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, πρὸ μὲν τοῦ πάθους ἁπαξαπλῶς φανέντος τοῖς πλείοσι καὶ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀεὶ. μετὰ δὲ τὸ πάθος οὐκέτι ὁμοίως ἐπιφαινομένου ἀλλὰ μετά τινος κρίσεως ἑκάστῳ μετρούσης τὰ δέοντα. ὥσπερ δ᾿ ἀναγέγραπται τὸ „ὤφθη ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραὰμ“ ἤ τινι τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ τὸ „ὤφθη“ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀεὶ ἐγίνετο ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ διαλειμμάτων, καὶ οὐ πᾶσιν ἐφαίνετο· οὕτω μοι νόει καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ὦφθαι τῇ παραπλησίᾳ περὶ ἐκείνων εἰς τὸ ὦφθαι αὐτοῖς τὸν θεὸν κρίσει.
pass_a_gloss: And do not wonder (μὴ θαύμαζε) if not all the crowds (ὄχλοι) who have believed (πεπιστευκότες) in Jesus see (βλέπουσιν, present) his resurrection, when (ὅτε), as to people not containing (μὴ χωροῦσι) more (πλείονα), Paul writing to Corinthians says: 'But I judged/decided (ἔκρινα) to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and this one crucified (ἐσταυρωμένον).' Of such kind (τοιοῦτον) is also the [saying]: 'For not yet (οὔπω) were you able; but not even yet now are you able, for you are still fleshly (σαρκικοί).' Thus then the word (ὁ λόγος), doing all things by divine judgement (κρίσει θείᾳ), wrote up (ἀνέγραψε) about Jesus: before the passion (πάθος) [he] having appeared simply/without distinction (ἁπαξαπλῶς) to the many (οἱ πλείονες), and this not always; but after the passion no longer appearing (ἐπιφαινομένου) in like manner, but with a certain judgement (κρίσις) measuring (μετρούσης) to each the things needed (τὰ δέοντα). And as is written up the 'God was seen (ὤφθη) by Abraham' or by one of the saints, and this 'was seen' did not happen always but at intervals (ἐκ διαλειμμάτων), and he did not appear to all; so, I pray, understand (μοι νόει) also the Son of God to have been seen by the like (παραπλησίᾳ) judgement as concerning those, for God's having been seen by them.
pass_b_english: And do not be surprised if not all the crowds who have believed in Jesus see his resurrection, when Paul, writing to the Corinthians as to people who could not take in more, says: “I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified” (1 Corinthians 2:2). Of the same kind is this saying too: “For you were not yet able; but even now you are still not able, for you are still fleshly” (1 Corinthians 3:2–3).

So the word, doing everything by divine judgement, has recorded of Jesus that before the passion he appeared to the many without distinction, and even this not always, but that after the passion he no longer showed himself in the same way, but with a certain judgement that measured out to each what was fitting. It is recorded that “God appeared to Abraham” (Genesis 12:7; compare 17:1; 18:1) or to one of the saints, and this “appeared” did not happen always but at intervals, nor did he appear to all. In just the same way, I ask you to understand that the Son of God also appeared by a judgement like the one by which God appeared to them.

choices.english: but even now you are still not able
choices.why: 1 Corinthians 3:2: ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν rendered 'but even now you are still not able' (was 'indeed').
ἁπαξαπλῶς: 'quite openly' -> 'without distinction' (set against the later measured judgement).
Genesis citation widened to 'Genesis 12:7; compare 17:1; 18:1' (LXX 18:1 has ὁ θεός; Origen's wording is general).

2.66: 'ὁ λόγος ... ἀνέγραψε' is kept as lowercase 'the word' (the Scripture account), with the translator note leaving open a reading as the divine Word. All five sections pass review, but the owner may want to settle this capitalisation.

translator_notes: ‘βλέπουσιν’ is present tense: Origen speaks of believers in general, not only eyewitnesses, so ‘see’ is kept in the present. ‘ὁ λόγος’ here most likely means the Christian word, i.e. the scriptural account (as in 2.68-69, where ‘ὁ λόγος’ is the account that records the truth); rendered lowercase ‘the word’. The phrase ‘doing everything by divine judgement’ could suit the divine Word inspiring Scripture; the lowercase rendering leaves that open without forcing it. ‘ἁπαξαπλῶς’ rendered ‘without distinction’ (lit. ‘simply, in general’), set against the later ‘with a certain judgement’. ‘ὤφθη ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ’: LXX Genesis 12:7 and 17:1 read ‘ὤφθη κύριος τῷ Αβραμ’, and LXX Genesis 18:1 ‘ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός’; Origen’s wording is a general paraphrase of these appearances; cited to Genesis 12:7 (compare 17:1; 18:1). ‘μοι νόει’ (ethical dative) rendered ‘I ask you to understand’. The last clause ‘τῇ παραπλησίᾳ περὶ ἐκείνων εἰς τὸ ὦφθαι αὐτοῖς τὸν θεὸν κρίσει’ is compressed; rendered by sense. Reviewer: Genesis citation shown inline as ‘Genesis 12:7; compare 17:1; 18:1’.
